requirements.text: the oldest incident that is still unresolved and currently assigned to this group must be escalated by setting its impact, urgency, and priority to their highest available levels
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_004' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical'
assumptions: the group is GROUP_001 (Level 1 Support Team, type IT Support), the only IT Support group that is a level 1 team; GROUP_003 shares the type but is the general IT Support Team
unresolved read as status not resolved and not closed: GROUP_001 then holds INC_004, INC_003, INC_014 and INC_016, all in status new
oldest read as earliest created_at: INC_004 (2024-02-18 09:30) is earlier than INC_003 (2024-02-19 10:00) although its id and number are higher
highest levels are the top of the policy enumerations: impact high, urgency high, priority critical, which the policy's impact x urgency matrix also gives
impact and urgency are already high on the seed; the requirement fails there only because priority is high, not critical

notes:
disagreement: missing requirement: one pass adds a stay that no notification with either report's subject is attached to an incident other than INC_004 (expected 0), the other has none; dropped because the reports are fixed by incident and recipient, the boundary of the incident selector is carried by the two incident stays, and the request forbids nothing about other incidents' notifications.
disagreement: value: the incident boundary stays' selector, one stay over GROUP_001 and GROUP_003 incidents of any status in one pass and two stays over unresolved incidents only in the other; chose one stay per group over incidents of any status, since the older resolved INC_001 and the closed INC_013 are what a reading that ignores 'still unresolved' would sweep in.
disagreement: value: the incident boundary stays' cells, priority critical only in one pass and any of impact, urgency or priority at its highest level in the other; chose all three cells, since the request escalates all three and a raise in any one of them on another incident is the error the stay guards.
The acting user, USER_001, is an active admin, so the update and both notifications are within scope. The incident table has no escalation flag; the request defines the escalation as the impact, urgency and priority change, so no other incident cell is tested. INC_004 already has impact and urgency high but priority high on the seed, out of line with the policy matrix, so the escalation shows only in priority. The assignee of INC_004, USER_006, is a member of GROUP_002, not GROUP_001; the request asks only to notify the current assignee and does not touch the assignment, so this seed inconsistency changes no requirement. Notification status and org_id are fixed by neither the request nor the policy and are not tested. Phrases of the request that the benchmark's keyword lists do not test (the reporter's incident being 'promoted') are not added as keywords, since a correct message may word them differently. The message keywords use LOWER(message) as the benchmark does; SQLite LIKE is case-insensitive for ASCII, so the cells' LIKE predicates are equivalent.
